name: reference
note: The headline cross-subject table: the encoder against every reference architecture, on one identical recipe, Cho2017 + Euclidean Alignment, 10 paired folds. val_frac is 0.0 deliberately -- a 20% carve with final-epoch selection removes trials from training and reads on nothing, and it costs roughly 1.9 points. Every arm here pays the same recipe, so the comparison is internally valid; it is a statement about architecture under THIS recipe, not about each architecture's best achievable number.

arms.name: ours
arms.prediction: the unmodified trunk; the reference every other arm is paired against

arms.name: ours_norm
arms.prediction: +1 to +2 over ours. Adding the one component every reference architecture has and this trunk lacks; it also unlocks test-time BN adaptation, which no-normalization forecloses entirely.

arms.name: ours_norm_samepad
arms.prediction: small further gain. Removes a real defect: the two branches emit different lengths and one is resampled onto the other, so index t means a different latency in each half of the embedding.

arms.name: ours_multiscale
arms.prediction: the largest single architectural gain. The trunk spans its scale range by dilation alone and has nothing short; four explicit kernels is the front end of the arm that currently beats it.

arms.name: ours_attn
arms.prediction: near parity. Attention costs accuracy when training data is scarce and turns mildly positive at this cohort size; 690 tokens for a sequence that is ~99% redundant is the reason it is not more.

arms.name: msvtnet
arms.prediction: currently the strongest baseline on this cell

arms.name: atcnet
arms.prediction: below its published figure; the published LOSO number is best-epoch-on-test

arms.name: riemann
arms.prediction: strong within-subject, weak across subjects: the tangent space is taken around a subject-specific reference

arms.name: null
arms.prediction: must land inside the chance band. Anything else means labels leak, and no other row in this table can be trusted.
